QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Landscape and Types_4

question.text: The IC of Vindhya Debt AIF is setting the hurdle rate for a new scheme. Based on the chapter's build-up: real risk-free rate = 2%, expected inflation = 6%, and the IC adds a risk premium of 4% over the nominal risk-free rate to compensate for credit risk on unrated mezzanine paper. Using the Fisher-type compounding relationship shown in the chapter for the nominal risk-free rate, what is the required rate of return (rounded to two decimals)?

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter computes nominal risk-free rate as NRR = [(1+real) x (1+inflation)] - 1 = (1.02)(1.06) - 1 = 0.0812 = 8.12%. The required rate of return is NRR plus the risk premium: 8.12% + 4% = 12.12%. That matches option A. The chapter's own worked example uses exactly these 2% and 6% numbers, producing the 8.12% nominal risk-free intermediate step. The Trap: (B) 12.00% uses simple addition (2+6+4) without the Fisher cross-term. (C) 12.32% wrongly compounds the risk premium into the Fisher formula — risk premium is added, not compounded, to NRR. (D) 10.12% omits the risk premium entirely (just 8.12% + 2%). Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) uses the same Fisher decomposition for hurdle setting. XV (Research Analyst) applies it in CAPM/cost-of-equity build-up. XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) covers the same formula in the shared foundational chapter. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting a Cat I/II PPM's preferred-return/hurdle clause, show the component build-up to LPs: real rate + inflation (Fisher) + illiquidity/credit premium. Hurdles quoted as flat 8% often mask the inflation assumption — if inflation spikes, your LP's real hurdle shrinks and catch-up economics shift.
